sn48.40:1.1: Here the faculties are correlated with the absorptions, highlighting the connection between the feelings and the practice of the path. | The title, according to the commentary, refers to the fact that the faculties are presented in the order in which they are abandoned through the development of absorption, rather than in the normal teaching sequence.
sn48.40:1.4: They experience pain in the body while meditating. | Each section pivots on the use of the verb uppajjati (“arise”) in present tense, past participle, and future tense.
sn48.40:1.6: Here nimitta clearly means “basis”, as also at eg. AN 2.77.
sn48.40:2.1: The sense of this is unclear. Perhaps as the meditator’s first absorption weakens they become conscious of how close the suffering of the sensory world is, and long for higher states. The commentary, instead, connects this sadness with the vitakka and vicāra that are still operating at this point. These are not in themselves unpleasant, but perhaps they are considered so because they are relatively unpeaceful.
sn48.40:3.1: Here the faculty of “pleasure” (sukha) seems to be equated with “rapture” (pīti), and “happiness” (somanassa) with “bliss” (also sukha).
